evidence: Quick independent Design-only solution-design review of specs/spec.md, design/design.md, design/contract.json, the cited pinned current-state seams, and the verified Python reference. The selected native-authority quarantine is grounded, proportional, numerically bounded, and mapped to failing-capable validation, but the machine-readable integration dependency graph cannot realize its own stated rollout order.

findings.issue: The integration lane omits AC2 even though its rule requires all seven leaf APIs to be green, and it depends on completed AC7 even though AC7 end-to-end validation requires the terminal and shared adapters this integration lane connects.
findings.why: This creates both an early-start hole and a dependency cycle: a planner following depends_on may integrate before the Design-sweep leaf is ready, or wait forever for AC7 completion that cannot occur until integration has shipped. Plan cannot decompose this Design without inventing a different milestone graph.
findings.suggestion: Replace acceptance-outcome dependencies with explicit leaf-readiness receipts for all seven lanes, including AC2. Make the integration lane depend on those implementation receipts, then make AC7 end-to-end checkout/finalization acceptance depend on the integration receipt; align the pair map and design/design.md sequence to those same milestones.

references_applied.application: Verified synchronous ownership, trust-boundary validation, separation of domain owners from transition adapters, no new runtime dependency or global locator, package-content coverage, and whether the proposed Python work can be decomposed without an unresolved sequencing decision.
